text:
maria: quick heads-up — I ran a set of KV + prefix-cache load tests this morning. mixing synthetic traffic with a deterministic replay harness (50/50). wanted to share surprising findings and get eyes.

bench-bot: started run id 20260319-1 (replay+synthetic, concurrency=64, reservoir=256MB) :rocket:

aj: nice — any config diff from the last run?

maria: same seed as last replay but changed eviction policy matrix: LRU, CLOCK, segLRU. batching heuristics set to dynamic (auto window) to simulate PLG burstiness. kernel selection on auto (we collect kernel_count per op).

maria: command used:
```
./bench --replay=apples --mix=50:50 --concurrency=64 --batch=dynamic --kernels=auto --cache-size=256MB --policies=LRU,CLOCK,segLRU
```

tariq: what metrics did you capture? hit rates / warmup / eviction churn?

maria: captured: per-policy hit_rate over time, warmup_seconds (time to reach 90% of steady hit rate), eviction_rate (evictions/sec), p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput (reqs/sec), kernel-selection counts, batch-size distribution, and a lightweight lock contention profile around kv store. also saved full flamegraph: https://artifacts.internal/runs/20260319-1/flamegraph.svg

maria: short summary (steady-state window):
- LRU: hit_rate=0.78, eviction_rate=0.028/s, warmup=22s, p99=118ms
- CLOCK: hit_rate=0.82, eviction_rate=0.035/s, warmup=47s, p99=130ms
- segLRU: hit_rate=0.80, eviction_rate=0.020/s, warmup=30s, p99=125ms

aj: CLOCK wins steady hit rate but much slower warmup — interesting. any idea why warmup regresses?

maria: profiling + traces point to two things:
1) kernel selection favored a heavier matmul kernel for longer sequences during CLOCK warmup which increased single-token latency. kernel_counts: heavy_kernel=14%, fast_kernel=86% in LRU vs heavy_kernel=32% in CLOCK during first 60s.
2) eviction churn higher initially for CLOCK because our clock hand scanning checks more tags per miss under bursty arrivals, causing more cache thrash before steady-state. lock contention on the clock-hand index shows spikes in the flamegraph.

aj: that suggests batching heuristics interact with policy during warmup. when batch sizes grow, the runtime picks a kernel optimized for throughput which in combination with clock's early churn gives worse p99.

maria: exactly. we also saw a weird corner: increasing cache size to 512MB made warmup even slower for CLOCK (surprising) — apparently because the larger address space made the clock hand traverse more entries before stabilizing, so the initial miss-paths touched more items and caused more disk-backed async loads in our sim.

tariq: did you test correctness under concurrency? any false hits/corruption?

maria: we added a concurrency correctness harness: 256 concurrent clients with interleaved prefix writes and reads, deterministic sequences. found a race in the eviction path where a stale tag could be observed simultaneously by a reader and the eviction worker, leading to an off-by-one hit accounting (not data corruption). reproduced reliably with seed=42.

maria: snippet from the failing trace:
```
[worker-evict] evict idx=10234 tag=0x7f8a mark->in-flight
[reader-64] lookup idx=10234 sees tag=0x0 (race) returns miss
[worker-evict] complete evict remove entry
[reader-64] later attempts write -> double-insert path exercised
```

sre-bot: alert created: KV-EVICT-RACE-20260319 (link: https://issues.internal/KV-1423)

aj: good catch. sounds like we need atomic tag transitions or a small CAS around the tag state. also we should expose per-entry state metrics to help diagnosis (in-flight / pinned / clean).

maria: agreed. proposed actions:
- tariq: add CAS-protected transitions for eviction/reader state and run the concurrency harness across 1k runs.
- aj: add per-entry metrics and a heatmap for clock-hand movement to the console.
- maria: refine benchmark to include a "gradual warmup" mode (start cache prefilled with sampled prefixes) so we can separate algorithmic warmup from population effects.

tariq: will do. also want to try a hybrid policy: CLOCK for steady-state with an LRU-like probation queue to speed warmup. may reduce initial churn.

aj: can you attach the raw CSVs? I'll run apples-vs-synthetic apples-to-apples comparison and plot p99 vs time.

maria: uploaded run artifacts here: https://artifacts.internal/runs/20260319-1/. csvs: hit_rate_timeseries.csv, eviction_timeseries.csv, kernel_counts.csv, batch_distribution.csv

maria: one more oddity — batching heuristics: when we disabled dynamic batching (forced batch=1) CLOCK had similar warmup to LRU but much lower throughput. that confirms the batching->kernel->policy interaction.

aj: plan: reproduce with single-run that toggles batching window width, measure kernel selection and p99 over warmup. need to ensure runs are identical seeds and same replay ordering (apples replay).

maria: putting a tiny checklist: 
- [x] baseline runs (LRU/CLOCK/segLRU)
- [x] concurrency correctness harness (repro seed attached)
- [x] artifacts uploaded
- [ ] implement CAS transitions (tariq)
- [ ] add per-entry metrics (aj)
- [ ] warmup-mode benchmark to isolate population effects (maria)

tariq: noting that kernel-selection telemetry needs higher resolution (per-batch) — adding an extra tag on the profiling path.

aj: thanks — :eyes: on the artifacts now. will share a quick plot in this thread when done.

maria: thanks all. if anyone wants to run extra policy candidates, add to the matrix and ping bench-bot with run-id.

bench-bot: run id 20260319-2 queued by @aj (policy=hybrid-clock-lru, concurrency=64)

aj: cool, I'll kick that off and post results.
